note: Faithful rule manifest. The .md is authoritative and unchanged; this indexes every actionable rule in it, typed checkable|judgment|principle, with a predicate (checkable) or proxy/reviewer criterion (judgment). No rule in the source is dropped — see sections_accounted.

schema.section: source section the rule comes from
schema.text: faithful statement of the rule (same meaning as the source)
schema.type: checkable = a program can verify it | judgment = needs the independent reviewer | principle = governing rationale, not per-artifact checkable
schema.predicate: checkable only: {kind, spec} the hook evaluates against produced artifacts
schema.reviewer_criterion: judgment only: the yes/no question the independent LLM-reviewer answers

rules.text: Determinism lives outside the forward pass: maximize the fraction of expertise expressed as a mechanically-checkable predicate, guarantee those in the harness, and route the irreducibly-semantic remainder to an independent grounded critic (raised + audited).
Decompose expertise into scoped, positively-framed, ID'd imperative rules. Say 'apply to every X', never 'apply generally'. Give each rule a stable ID.

predicate.spec: the built agent's expertise has a manifest with ID'd rules; each rule text is imperative and scoped (no bare 'apply generally').

rules.text: Compile each rule into a bucket: (a) mechanically-checkable predicate -> harness gate (preferred), or (b) semantic rubric item -> independent grounded judge.

predicate.spec: every rule in the manifest has type in {checkable,judgment}; checkable rules carry a predicate, judgment rules carry a reviewer_criterion.

rules.text: Force the agent to CITE the governing rule-IDs before/at finishing, turning 'consulted the rule' into a checkable artifact.

predicate.spec: the agent emits APPLIED-EXPERTISE: <name>#<rule-ids> naming the concrete rule ids it applied (not just the expertise name).

rules.text: Re-assert the top rules at the TAIL before consequential actions and every few turns, cache-safe (in-messages system entries / UserPromptSubmit / PreToolUse surfacing). Fights decay without cache-bust.

predicate.spec: a PreToolUse (gate) surfaces the relevant rules before a Write/Edit, and/or a per-turn re-assert hook is wired — not SessionStart-only.

rules.text: Review must be independent, grounded, and fail-closed: a SEPARATE agent judges; never self-grade; ground on the expertise text + artifacts; may only block.

predicate.spec: the reviewer is a different agent/model from the author (never the same instance grading its own work) and its verdict can only block, never certify success.

rules.text: Govern outputs and actions, not the reasoning trace. Never phrase a rule as 'in your thinking...'.

predicate.spec: no rule text targets the private reasoning trace (reject phrasings like 'in your thinking', 'in your reasoning', 'in your extended thinking').

rules.text: Self-critique helps ONLY as a visible output step grounded on external evidence (test/validator/retrieved rule/independent judge). Never intrinsic self-critique; never instructions aimed at the hidden reasoning trace.

predicate.spec: any self-critique/repair loop checks the output against an external artifact (test result / validator output / retrieved rule), not the model's unaided opinion.

rules.text: An LLM-as-judge must be INDEPENDENT (never self-grade), evidence-grounded, and fail-closed; a 'pass' is never proof of success — prove success with deterministic checks.

predicate.spec: the judge model is cross-family / a different instance from the author; grounded on the expertise text + artifacts; can only block; success is proven by deterministic checks, not the judge's 'pass'.

rules.text: Keep an immutable high expertise prefix (cache + primacy) AND tail re-assertion (in-messages entries, no cache-bust) — use both edges of the attention curve.

predicate.spec: the stable expertise is injected high/immutable (SessionStart) and the top rules are re-asserted at the tail before risky steps.

rules.text: Measure per-rule adherence rate: deterministic checks for bucket-(a), independent-judge rate for bucket-(b), plus a multi-turn-stability slice. Stop ASSUMING application — measure it.

predicate.spec: an adherence log + per-rule adherence report exists and is produced over time (not a one-off).

rules.text: Honest limit: constrained decoding / a declaration guarantees FORM, not correctness — a schema forces a rule_id field, not the RIGHT rule, and a bare declaration token does not prove the rule was applied. Verify the artifact embodies the rule, not just that the token exists.
Honest limit: the gate-checkable / raise-the-rest split is reasoned, not benchmarked (gap G2: no head-to-head of prompt-raise vs hard-gate on one ruleset). Do not oversell 'proven'.
